notes: dc CALL 2026-10-29 Q3 2026 call: CFO Ling Hai, CEO Michael Miebach; transcript read through a WebFetch summary of the Motley Fool copy (search_excerpt, not the full verbatim transcript); Alpha Vantage EARNINGS_CALL_TRANSCRIPT probe was rate-limited (25/day), not retried.

dc MGMT (call) full-year net revenue growth 'at the high end of the low double digits range' currency-neutral, excluding inorganic activity; Q2 call had already moved expectations higher in the range; Q4 same wording; ~1 ppt FX tailwind FY, ~1 ppt FX headwind Q4. Words are management's; the numeric 12-13% in guidance rows is my reading of the words.

dc MGMT (call) Q4: slight revenue headwind from timing of services projects and network deals pulled forward into Q3; 'similar offset' in VAS in Q4; rebates and incentives as % of gross assessments higher than Q3; no full-year rebates guidance given. Not addressed: litigation, capex, operating margin outlook; 2027 guidance comes with the next quarter's release.

dc MGMT (call) cross-border travel 'similar to the end of Q2'; agentic commerce expected to build with holiday shopping (CEO); BVNK impact on Q3 VAS 'minimal'; opex FY 'low double digits' unchanged, Q4 high end of low double digits with 1 ppt drag from acquisitions; non-GAAP tax 20-21%; Q4 other expense ~ $115m.
dc MGMT (release) CEO Miebach: Agentic Commerce, new Global Money Platform through BVNK (stablecoin infrastructure, acquired 2026-08-03 for $1.4bn cash plus up to $300m contingent).

dc Q3 RESULT (released 2026-10-29, citable from 2026-10-31): net revenue $9,807m +14% (reported and currency-neutral; payment network +11%, VAS +19%), GDV +7% local to $2.95tn, cross-border volume +11%, switched transactions +9%, GAAP operating margin 59.8% (+0.9 ppt), adjusted 60.5%, adjusted EPS $5.31 (+21%), GAAP EPS $5.28; adjusted opex +12% (1 ppt acquisitions).

dc REBATES Q3 rebates and incentives $6,369m +18% (9M $18,005m +21%), growing faster than payment network net revenue (+11%) and than GDV (+7%); the release cites new and renewed deals. Share of gross network assessments 52.6% in Q3 2026 vs 51.3% FY2025 (derived).

dc CASH conversion 9M 2026 operating cash flow $11,859m vs $12,646m (-6%) while net income +18%: prepaid expenses (customer incentive prepayments) outflow $4,688m vs $2,939m; amortization of customer incentives $2,030m vs $1,526m; accrued litigation payments $537m. Gap to be read by the analyst; capex+software $1,141m 9M.

dc LITIGATION provision for litigation Q3 $74m (settlements with opt-out merchants in U.S. interchange case) vs $83m, 9M $156m vs $330m; accrued litigation fell to $262m from $800m (cash settlements paid). Block and Intuit remain unsettled opt-outs seeking aggregate single damages above $5bn (summary judgment briefing continues through 2026); Rules Relief Class revised settlement preliminarily approved June 2026, final approval hearing November 2026; Damages Class release upheld Sept 2026 against April 2026 putative class action (appeal to Second Circuit); U.S. EMV liability shift class alleges >$1bn single damages against four networks (10-Q Note 14).

dc LITIGATION UK October 2026: two new proposed UK collective actions served: ~GBP 1.5bn (domestic and cross-border consumer transactions) and ~GBP 0.4bn (online cross-border); existing UK commercial card claim >GBP 1bn; Portugal ~EUR 0.4bn; Netherlands ~EUR 0.3bn; Australia ACCC debit agreements, liability hearing concluded June 2026; ATM operator opt-out settled Aug 2026 and ATM operators class dismissed Sept 2026 (10-Q Note 14). Claimed amounts are plaintiffs' claims, not accruals; the 10-Q accrual is $262m.

dc LITIGATION DOJ: Civil Investigative Demand received 2023 from DOJ Antitrust Division on U.S. debit program competition (Sherman Act 1 or 2); company cooperating (10-K, Legal Proceedings; the Q3 10-Q text prefetched contains no separate DOJ paragraph). European Commission request for information (2024) on network fees related to acquirers; cooperating.

dc ONEOFFS Q3 2026 special item: litigation provisions $74m pre-tax (adjusted net income effect +$49m); equity investments net pre-tax loss $5m (adjusted net income effect -$24m per release reconciliation, including tax effects); YTD special items: restructuring $202m (Q1 2026) and litigation $156m; adjusted tax rate 20.1% vs GAAP 19.4% in Q3.

dc RISK interchange and merchant acceptance-cost activity, surcharging limits and litigation could cut revenue or raise incentive costs (10-K Item 1A, Legal and Regulatory: interchange, surcharging, litigation liabilities).
dc RISK preferential or protective government actions favouring domestic payment networks, and regulation of privacy, data and AI (10-K Item 1A, Legal and Regulatory).
dc RISK competition and disintermediation: account-based and real-time payments, wallets, stablecoins, Visa and others; continued intense pricing pressure (10-K Item 1A, Business: Competition).

dc RISK customer concentration: five largest customers about 21% of FY2025 net revenue ($6.9bn); loss of a large customer or card program and consolidation; incentives rise with renewals (10-K Item 1A, Business: customers; Item 7 notes).
dc RISK global economy, cross-border travel and spending sensitivity, tariffs and trade policy, currency and FX controls (10-K Item 1A, Global events).
dc RISK settlement guarantor exposure and information security incidents, service disruptions (10-K Item 1A, Operational).
dc RISK acquisition integration and entry into new businesses, stablecoin and account-based payments (BVNK) (10-K Item 1A; 10-Q Note 2).

dc GAP full transcript Q&A not read verbatim (summary of Motley Fool copy only); no customer-level names or per-customer shares disclosed (only top-5 aggregate); no segment operating income (single reportable segment, cannot be split between payment network and VAS); remaining performance obligations, backlog and purchase commitments not extracted (not material to this model); Q2 numeric prior guidance not available as numbers (words only), so prior_low/prior_high left empty.
